style.vernacular: Highland capital at about 2,355 m: a patchwork of 1-3 storey painted-render and concrete houses with rust-red or galvanised corrugated-iron roofs, scattered Italian-era (1936-41) arcaded blocks around Piazza and Churchill Avenue, mid-century modernist ministries and campuses from the Haile Selassie era, Derg-era concrete squares, and a recent boom of glass-and-concrete towers, malls and apartment blocks wrapped in eucalyptus-pole scaffolding. Traditional round tukul and chika (mud-and-straw) houses survive on the edges. Eucalyptus trees (planted from Menelik II onward) line streets and hillsides.
style.ornament: Ethiopian Orthodox crosses and round/octagonal church plans with concentric ambulatories; Aksumite-inspired stepped stone banding and stelae motifs on state buildings; green-yellow-red tricolour trims; Italian-era arcades and rationalist corners around Piazza; lion-of-Judah statuary; corrugated-iron fence sheets and eucalyptus scaffolding around construction sites.

sources.what: highland capital, mix of eras, construction boom of towers and malls
early mud-and-thatch round huts, Menelik II eucalyptus planting, Italian occupation planning with European-style axes, later modernist plans, tower boom, Sheger Park/Riverside greening
